title: Functions & Slope
subtitle: Rate of Change, Start Value, y = mx + b
bounds: PROTOCOL §4b Coordinates and lines. Coordinates in a prompt are integers of size <= 10; every table value, input and output is an integer of size <= 20 (tables have 3 rows; T1 pairs use 0-9). Slopes and rates: an integer of size 2-10, or a simplest fraction a/b with a, b <= 5 and a/b != 1; rise and run each of size <= 10 (run >= 2) and the division exact or a times-table fact (rise = g*a, run = g*b). Every y = mx + b has m and b nonzero integers of size <= 10 (T1 rule evaluation: m 2-5, input 1-6, output 1-20). Unit rate k 2-5 with x*k <= 10; compared rates are integers 2-9. Equations use only x to the first power except the not-linear examples (x^2, x^3, 2^x). No f(x), no graphs, no domain and range. Wrong choices may be any size <= 999.

tiers.name: Is It a Function?
tiers.description: One input, one output: spot functions, then plug in a rule.

tiers.name: Slope & Rate of Change
tiers.description: Rise over run from points, tables and stories.

tiers.description: Lines, curves, rising and falling, steady steps.

REPEAT_OUTPUT.student: Outputs may repeat. Only one input with two outputs breaks it.
REPEAT_OUTPUT.teacher: Says a repeated output means not a function (reads the rule backwards).

REPEAT_INPUT_OK.student: One input can't have two outputs. That's what breaks a function.
REPEAT_INPUT_OK.teacher: Accepts an input that is paired with two different outputs as a function.

INPUT_OUTPUT_SWAP.student: Inputs go in, outputs come out. The input is x, the output is y.
INPUT_OUTPUT_SWAP.teacher: Swaps input and output: tests the second number for repeats, or solves for x instead of y.

PLUGGED_WRONG.student: Do the steps in the order the rule says, one at a time.
PLUGGED_WRONG.teacher: Applies the rule's steps in the wrong order, or puts the constant inside the product.

ADDED_PARTS.student: Multiply where it says multiply. Don't just add every number.
ADDED_PARTS.teacher: Adds slope, input and constant instead of multiplying the input by the slope.

STOPPED_EARLY.student: Finish both steps of the rule: multiply, then add or subtract.
STOPPED_EARLY.teacher: Does only the first step of a two-step rule.

RUN_OVER_RISE.student: Slope is rise over run: the up-down change goes on top.
RUN_OVER_RISE.teacher: Divides run by rise, the reciprocal of the slope.

SIGN_SLIP.student: Check the sign: going down as x goes up means a negative slope.
SIGN_SLIP.teacher: Right size, wrong sign on a slope or rate of change.

RISE_ONLY.student: Divide by the run too. Slope is the rise over the run.
RISE_ONLY.teacher: Reports the change in y and never divides by the change in x.

START_AS_RATE.student: The first y is where it starts. The rate is the change per step.
START_AS_RATE.teacher: Reads the first y value in a table or story as the rate of change.

TOTAL_CHANGE.student: Rate is the change for 1 step of x, not across the whole table.
TOTAL_CHANGE.teacher: Uses the change from the first to the last row instead of the change per unit of x.

ADDED_RISE_RUN.student: Slope divides rise by run. Adding them doesn't give a rate.
ADDED_RISE_RUN.teacher: Adds rise and run instead of dividing.

SLOPE_AS_START.student: The number with x is the slope. The start is the lone number.
SLOPE_AS_START.teacher: Reports the coefficient of x as the initial value (or its absolute value, or m + b).

START_AS_SLOPE.student: The slope is the number multiplying x, not the one added.
START_AS_SLOPE.teacher: Reports the constant term as the slope.

VALUE_AT_1.student: Start means x = 0, not x = 1. Back up one step to find it.
VALUE_AT_1.teacher: Uses y at x = 1 (or the first table value) as the initial value.

SIGN_DROPPED.student: Keep the minus sign. It belongs to the number after it.
SIGN_DROPPED.teacher: Drops a negative sign on the slope or the start value.

SWAPPED_MB.student: The slope goes with x. The start is the number you add.
SWAPPED_MB.teacher: Swaps m and b in y = mx + b.

NO_START.student: Include the starting amount: y = rate × x + start.
NO_START.teacher: Writes y = mx and leaves out the initial value.

LAST_VALUE.student: The start is y at x = 0, not the last y in the table.
LAST_VALUE.teacher: Uses the last table value as the initial value.

BIGGER_TOTAL.student: Compare rates, not totals: divide each total by its time.
BIGGER_TOTAL.teacher: Picks the case with the bigger headline number instead of the bigger rate.

INVERTED_RATE.student: Rate is amount per 1 unit: divide the amount by the units.
INVERTED_RATE.teacher: Divides the units by the amount (or x by y), the reciprocal of the rate.

START_NOT_RATE.student: Speed is the slope, the number with x. A big start isn't speed.
START_NOT_RATE.teacher: Compares starting amounts (the constants) instead of the rates of change.

DIFFERENCE.student: Unit rate is y ÷ x, not y − x.
DIFFERENCE.teacher: Subtracts y − x to get the rate.

TOTAL_AS_RATE.student: Unit rate is for 1 x, so divide y by x.
TOTAL_AS_RATE.teacher: Reports y itself as the unit rate.

HAS_START.student: Proportional lines have no added number: y = kx exactly.
HAS_START.teacher: Treats y = kx + c as proportional (ignores the constant).

ADDS_NOT_MULTIPLIES.student: Proportional means y = kx (multiply), not y = x + k.
ADDS_NOT_MULTIPLIES.teacher: Treats a constant difference (y = x + k) as proportional.

STEADY_MEANS_PROP.student: Steady steps aren't enough. y ÷ x must match in every row.
STEADY_MEANS_PROP.teacher: Calls a table proportional because y rises by equal steps (ignores the ratio).

NEEDS_ZERO_ROW.student: No x = 0 row needed. Check that y ÷ x is the same each row.
NEEDS_ZERO_ROW.teacher: Says a table with constant ratio is not proportional because it lacks (0, 0).

CONSTANT_NOT_LINEAR.student: Adding a number still makes a line: y = mx + b is linear.
CONSTANT_NOT_LINEAR.teacher: Says y = mx + b (b nonzero) is not linear.

MINUS_NOT_LINEAR.student: A minus sign still makes a line. It slopes down or shifts.
MINUS_NOT_LINEAR.teacher: Says an equation with subtraction or a negative slope is not linear.

EXPONENT_IGNORED.student: A power of x (x^2, 2^x) bends the graph. Linear is x to the 1st.
EXPONENT_IGNORED.teacher: Ignores the exponent and calls a squared, cubed or exponential rule linear.

CONSTANT_SIGN_DECIDES.student: The number multiplying x sets the direction, not the added one.
CONSTANT_SIGN_DECIDES.teacher: Decides rising or falling from the sign of the constant term.

SLOPE_SIGN_IGNORED.student: Slope sign: positive y rises, negative falls, zero stays put.
SLOPE_SIGN_IGNORED.teacher: Picks a direction that disagrees with the sign of the slope.

CONSTANT_RATE_MEANS_SAME.student: A steady rate still moves y. It stays put only if the slope is 0.
CONSTANT_RATE_MEANS_SAME.teacher: Reads a constant rate of change as y staying the same.

EQUAL_STEPS_MISSED.student: Uneven x steps are fine. Check that y changes at a steady rate.
EQUAL_STEPS_MISSED.teacher: Says a table with uneven x gaps is not linear (compares y steps only).

DECREASING_NOT_LINEAR.student: Going down steadily is still a line, with a negative slope.
DECREASING_NOT_LINEAR.teacher: Says a steadily decreasing table is not linear.

LOOKS_GROWING.student: Going up isn't enough. The steps in y must match the steps in x.
LOOKS_GROWING.teacher: Calls any increasing table linear without checking for a constant rate.

SAME_NOT_CHECKED.student: Work out both rates. They differ, so one is greater.
SAME_NOT_CHECKED.teacher: Says the two are the same without comparing the rates.

RATE_NOT_COMPARED.student: Work out both rates. Here they match, so it's a tie.
RATE_NOT_COMPARED.teacher: Picks one line when the rates are equal (compares something else).
